ful-medames.name: Ful medames
ful-medames.summary: A stew of cooked fava beans seasoned with olive oil and spices, considered Egypt's national dish and a staple food there since at least the 17th century.

koshary.name: Koshary
koshary.summary: Egypt's national dish and popular street food, mixing pasta, rice, vermicelli and lentils, topped with chickpeas, garlicky tomato sauce and crispy fried onions.

mulukhiyah.name: Mulukhiyah
mulukhiyah.summary: A traditional Egyptian and Arab dish made from the leaves of a jute plant, cooked into a thick, mucilaginous broth or stew and usually served with rice.

om-ali.name: Umm Ali
om-ali.summary: A traditional Egyptian dessert traced back to medieval Egypt, said to be named after a sultan's wife and commonly eaten during Ramadan.

basbousa.name: Basbousa
basbousa.summary: A syrup-soaked semolina dessert popular across the Middle East, North Africa, the Caucasus and the Balkans.

falafel.name: Tamiya
falafel.summary: The Sudanese name for falafel, a deep-fried ball made from ground beans and a popular Middle Eastern street food; in Sudan it is made with chickpeas rather than fava beans.

pastitsio.name: Pastitsio
pastitsio.summary: A baked pasta dish with ground meat and béchamel sauce from Greece's Ionian Islands, with variations found elsewhere around the Mediterranean.

lower-nubia.name: Lower Nubia
lower-nubia.summary: Northernmost part of ancient Nubia, now largely submerged under Lake Nasser after the Aswan High Dam's construction, with its monuments relocated in a major 20th-century rescue effort.

world-heritage-convention.name: World Heritage Convention
world-heritage-convention.summary: An international treaty signed in 1972 that created UNESCO's World Heritage Sites and set out how countries should identify, protect and conserve them.

neo-mamluk-architecture.name: Neo-Mamluk architecture
neo-mamluk-architecture.summary: An architectural style popular in Egypt from the late 19th to early 20th century, blending modern European design with historic Mamluk elements in government buildings, mosques and homes.

mamluk.name: Mamluks
mamluk.summary: Non-Arab enslaved soldiers, often of Turkic or Circassian origin, who converted to Islam and trained for war before being freed to serve as an elite military and political class in Egypt for nearly 1,000 years.

museum-of-modern-egyptian-art.name: Museum of Modern Egyptian Art
museum-of-modern-egyptian-art.summary: Cairo's main modern art museum, inaugurated in 1927, holding collections of early 20th-century Egyptian pioneers such as Mahmoud Said and Ragheb Ayad.

mahmoud-sa-id.name: Mahmoud Said
mahmoud-sa-id.summary: Egyptian judge and painter from Alexandria, who lived from 1897 to 1964.

gazbia-sirry.name: Gazbia Sirry
gazbia-sirry.summary: Egyptian painter (1925–2021) known for depicting women in poses of power and, from the late 1950s, increasingly abstract work reflecting Egypt's political mood.

abdel-hadi-al-gazzar.name: Abdel Hadi Al Gazzar
abdel-hadi-al-gazzar.summary: An Egyptian painter, living from 1925 to 1966, known for blending social commentary with traditional Egyptian identity, notably in his painting The High Dam.

abu-simbel.name: Abu Simbel temples
abu-simbel.summary: Two rock-cut temples in Upper Egypt carved in the 13th century BCE for Ramesses II, with giant statues of him and smaller figures of his wife Nefertari and children.

temple-of-debod.name: Temple of Debod
temple-of-debod.summary: An ancient Nubian temple built in the early 2nd century BC near Aswan, given by Egypt to Spain in 1968 and rebuilt in a Madrid park in 1970-72.

ramses-wissa-wassef.name: Ramses Wissa Wassef
ramses-wissa-wassef.summary: Egyptian architect and art professor (1911–1974) who drew on Pharaonic, Coptic and Islamic traditions and founded an art center that revived an ancient weaving technique.

wael-shawky.name: Wael Shawky
wael-shawky.summary: Egyptian artist, born 1971, known internationally for works retelling the history of the Crusades from a Middle Eastern perspective, winner of several major art prizes.

mohammed-wardi.name: Mohammed Wardi
mohammed-wardi.summary: Nubian Sudanese singer, poet and songwriter (1932–2012) regarded as a cultural icon of modern Sudan and a voice of its political and social consciousness.

wadi-halfa.name: Wadi Halfa
wadi-halfa.summary: A city in northern Sudan near the Egyptian border, surrounded by ancient Nubian sites and believed to be one of the oldest settlements in the central Nile valley, dating to around 7000 BC.

abu-al-abbas-al-mursi-mosque.name: Abu al-Abbas al-Mursi Mosque
abu-al-abbas-al-mursi-mosque.summary: 13th-century mosque, mausoleum and Sufi shrine in Alexandria, Egypt, named for and housing the tomb of the mystic Abu'l Abbas al-Mursi.

mario-rossi-architect.name: Mario Rossi
mario-rossi-architect.summary: Italian architect (1897–1961) noted as a contributor to 20th-century Islamic architecture.

temple-of-taffeh.name: Temple of Taffeh
temple-of-taffeh.summary: A Roman-era Egyptian temple built between 25 BCE and 14 CE, later given to the Netherlands and now displayed in Leiden's Rijksmuseum van Oudheden.

temple-of-dendur.name: Temple of Dendur
temple-of-dendur.summary: A Roman-era Egyptian temple built around 23 BCE for the goddess Isis, rescued from Nile flooding in the 1960s and given to New York's Metropolitan Museum of Art.

temples-of-wadi-es-sebua.name: Wadi es-Sebua
temples-of-wadi-es-sebua.summary: A pair of New Kingdom Egyptian temples in Lower Nubia, including one built by Ramesses II, relocated in the 1960s during the campaign to save Nubia's monuments.

temple-of-beit-el-wali.name: Beit el-Wali
temple-of-beit-el-wali.summary: A rock-cut Egyptian temple in Nubia built by Ramesses II and dedicated to several gods, relocated in the 1960s as part of the Aswan High Dam rescue project.

el-alamein.name: El Alamein
el-alamein.summary: An Egyptian coastal city west of Alexandria, today known for oil and tourism, near which the First and Second Battles of El Alamein were fought.

gamal-abdel-nasser.name: Gamal Abdel Nasser
gamal-abdel-nasser.summary: Egypt's second president (1954–1970), who led the 1952 revolution, nationalized the Suez Canal, championed pan-Arab unity, and briefly united Egypt and Syria in the United Arab Republic.

first-sudanese-civil-war.name: First Sudanese Civil War
first-sudanese-civil-war.summary: A civil war fought from 1955 to 1972 between northern and southern Sudan over autonomy, killing around a million people before ending with the 1972 Addis Ababa Agreement.

second-sudanese-civil-war.name: Second Sudanese Civil War
second-sudanese-civil-war.summary: A conflict from 1983 to 2005 between Sudan's government and the Sudan People's Liberation Army that killed roughly two million people and led to South Sudan's independence.

war-in-darfur.name: War in Darfur
war-in-darfur.summary: A conflict beginning in 2003 when rebel groups fought Sudan's government, which responded with a campaign of ethnic cleansing against Darfur's non-Arab population, leading to genocide charges against President Omar al-Bashir.

anglo-egyptian-treaty-of-1936.name: 1936 Anglo-Egyptian Treaty
anglo-egyptian-treaty-of-1936.summary: A 1936 agreement that ended most British control over Egypt's internal affairs but let Britain keep about 10,000 troops near the Suez Canal and help train and defend Egypt's army for 20 years.

anwar-sadat.name: Anwar Sadat
anwar-sadat.summary: President of Egypt from 1970 to 1981 who led Egypt in the 1973 war against Israel and later negotiated the Camp David Accords and the Egypt–Israel peace treaty.

muammar-gaddafi.name: Muammar Gaddafi
muammar-gaddafi.summary: A Libyan military officer and revolutionary who ruled Libya from 1969, after a bloodless coup, until his overthrow and death in 2011.

yom-kippur-war.name: Yom Kippur War
yom-kippur-war.summary: 1973 war between Israel and a coalition led by Egypt and Syria, sparked by a surprise attack on the Jewish holy day of Yom Kippur, fought mainly in Sinai and the Golan Heights.

straits-of-tiran.name: Straits of Tiran
straits-of-tiran.summary: Narrow sea passages between the Sinai and Arabian peninsulas linking the Gulf of Aqaba to the Red Sea, whose blockade led to wars in 1956 and 1967.

farouk-of-egypt.name: Farouk of Egypt
farouk-of-egypt.summary: Tenth ruler of Egypt from the Muhammad Ali dynasty, reigning from 1936 until his overthrow in the 1952 coup; known for an extravagant lifestyle, he died in exile in 1965.

wafd-party.name: Wafd Party
wafd-party.summary: Egypt's most influential nationalist liberal political party from the end of World War I through the 1930s, key to shaping the 1923 constitution; dissolved in 1953.

egyptian-revolution-of-1952.name: Egyptian revolution of 1952
egyptian-revolution-of-1952.summary: A 1952 coup in which army officers led by Mohamed Naguib and Gamal Abdel Nasser toppled King Farouk, ending Egypt's monarchy and later founding a republic.

national-liberation-front-algeria.name: National Liberation Front (FLN)
national-liberation-front-algeria.summary: Algeria's dominant nationalist party since independence in 1962, formed in 1954 and the main force behind the Algerian War against French rule.

shimon-peres.name: Shimon Peres
shimon-peres.summary: Israeli politician and statesman (1923–2016) who served as prime minister twice and as president from 2007 to 2014, over a 70-year political career.

zakaria-mohieddin.name: Zakaria Mohieddin
zakaria-mohieddin.summary: Egyptian military officer and politician (1918–2012) who served as Egypt's 3rd prime minister and headed its first intelligence agency.

naguib-mahfouz.name: Naguib Mahfouz
naguib-mahfouz.summary: Egyptian writer (1911–2006) who won the 1988 Nobel Prize in Literature, the only Egyptian to do so, over a 70-year career of 35 novels.

ahmed-zewail.name: Ahmed Zewail
ahmed-zewail.summary: Egyptian-American chemist known as the father of femtochemistry, who won the 1999 Nobel Prize in Chemistry as the first Egyptian and Arab Nobel laureate in a scientific field.

galerie-68.name: Galerie 68
galerie-68.summary: An avant-garde Egyptian literary magazine based in Cairo, published 1968–1971 with a one-year gap, producing eight issues in total.

femtochemistry.name: Femtochemistry
femtochemistry.summary: Field of physical chemistry studying chemical reactions on femtosecond timescales, letting scientists watch atoms rearrange as reactions happen; Ahmed Zewail won the 1999 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for pioneering it.

damanhur.name: Damanhur
damanhur.summary: A historic city in Egypt's Nile Delta, capital of the Beheira Governorate, dating back to the Old Kingdom and birthplace of Nobel-winning chemist Ahmed Zewail.

early-dynastic-period-of-egypt.name: Early Dynastic Period (Egypt)
early-dynastic-period-of-egypt.summary: The era of ancient Egypt just after Upper and Lower Egypt were unified around 3150 BC, covering the First and Second Dynasties until about 2686 BC.

order-of-the-nile.name: Order of the Nile
order-of-the-nile.summary: Egypt's highest state honor, established in 1915 as one of the Kingdom's principal orders and reconstituted as the Republic's top decoration after the monarchy ended in 1953.

desouk.name: Disuq
desouk.summary: A city in northern Egypt about 80 km east of Alexandria, dating back to at least around 3200 BC and once part of the ancient city of Buto.

first-dynasty-of-egypt.name: First Dynasty of Egypt
first-dynasty-of-egypt.summary: First series of Egyptian kings to rule a unified Egypt, following the unification of Upper and Lower Egypt, dated to roughly the 32nd to 31st century BC.

minoan-eruption.name: Minoan eruption
minoan-eruption.summary: A massive volcanic eruption on Thera (Santorini) around 1600 BC that destroyed the Akrotiri settlement and nearby communities with earthquakes and tsunamis.

glasgow-chronology.name: Glasgow Chronology
glasgow-chronology.summary: A revision of ancient Egyptian chronology proposed between 1978 and 1982 by a Society for Interdisciplinary Studies working group, placing Egypt's Eighteenth Dynasty about five hundred years later than the conventional dating.

new-chronology-rohl.name: New Chronology (Rohl)
new-chronology-rohl.summary: An alternative, unaccepted revision of ancient Near Eastern chronology by Egyptologist David Rohl, re-dating Egyptian kings by up to 350 years to match them with biblical figures.

third-intermediate-period-of-egypt.name: Third Intermediate Period
third-intermediate-period-of-egypt.summary: A period of ancient Egyptian history running from the death of Ramesses XI in 1077 BCE to about 664 BCE, marked by political division, foreign rulers and instability.

muhammad-ali-dynasty.name: Muhammad Ali dynasty
muhammad-ali-dynasty.summary: The ruling house of Egypt and Sudan from the 19th to the mid-20th century, named after its founder Muhammad Ali Pasha.

fuad-ii-of-egypt.name: Fuad II
fuad-ii-of-egypt.summary: Infant member of Egypt's Muhammad Ali dynasty who briefly reigned as the last King of Egypt and the Sudan, from July 1952 until being deposed in June 1953.

mohamed-naguib.name: Mohamed Naguib
mohamed-naguib.summary: Egyptian officer who, with Gamal Abdel Nasser, led the Free Officers movement that toppled the monarchy in 1952; he served as Egypt's first president until Nasser forced his resignation in 1954.

1919-egyptian-revolution.name: 1919 Egyptian Revolution
1919-egyptian-revolution.summary: Nationwide Egyptian uprising against British occupation from November 1918 to July 1919, sparked by the exile of nationalist leader Saad Zaghloul; it paved the way toward Egypt's 1922 independence.

abbas-ii-of-egypt.name: Abbas II of Egypt
abbas-ii-of-egypt.summary: The last Khedive of Egypt and Sudan, ruling from 1892 to 1914, deposed by the British as a nationalist in favor of his more pro-British uncle after the Ottoman Empire joined World War I against Britain.

khedive.name: Khedive
khedive.summary: A Persian-origin honorific title used by Ottoman sultans and viziers, and most famously by Egypt's viceroys from 1805 to 1914, first claimed by Muhammad Ali Pasha and officially recognized by the Ottomans in 1867.

1948-arab-israeli-war.name: 1948 Arab–Israeli War
1948-arab-israeli-war.summary: Also called the First Arab-Israeli War, fought from May 1948 to March 1949 after Israel's declaration of independence, when a coalition of Arab states entered former Mandatory Palestine.

anglo-egyptian-sudan.name: Anglo-Egyptian Sudan
anglo-egyptian-sudan.summary: The joint British-Egyptian rule over Sudan from 1899 to 1956, in which Britain held effective control despite formally shared sovereignty, ending with Sudan's independence.

fuad-i-of-egypt.name: Fuad I
fuad-i-of-egypt.summary: Ruler of Egypt from 1917 to 1936, the last Sultan and first King of Egypt and the Sudan, who replaced the sultan title with king in 1922.

kosheh-massacres.name: Kosheh massacres
kosheh-massacres.summary: Killing of 21 Coptic Christians in Kosheh, Upper Egypt on 2 January 2000, considered martyrs by the Coptic Orthodox Church.

nag-hammadi-massacre.name: Nag Hammadi massacre
nag-hammadi-massacre.summary: A 2010 killing of six Coptic Christians and a police officer outside a cathedral in Nag Hammadi, Egypt, on Christmas Eve, one of Egypt's worst anti-Christian attacks since 2000.

2011-alexandria-bombing.name: 2011 Alexandria Bombing
2011-alexandria-bombing.summary: New Year's Day 2011 bombing of a Coptic church in Alexandria, Egypt, that killed 23 people, the deadliest attack on Egypt's Copts in a decade.

huda-sha-arawi.name: Huda Sha'arawi
huda-sha-arawi.summary: Egyptian feminist leader, suffragette and nationalist (1879–1947) who founded the Egyptian Feminist Union.

coptic-orthodox-church.name: Coptic Orthodox Church
coptic-orthodox-church.summary: An Oriental Orthodox Christian church based in Egypt, traditionally founded by Saint Mark around AD 42, and the largest Christian group in Egypt and the Middle East.

bah-faith.name: Baháʼí Faith
bah-faith.summary: A religion founded by Baháʼu'lláh in 19th-century Iran teaching the unity of all religions and people, with 7 to 8 million followers worldwide today.

arab-barometer.name: Arab Barometer
arab-barometer.summary: A nonpartisan research network that has run public opinion surveys across the Arab world since 2006, run with Princeton and Michigan universities and regional partners.

kemetism.name: Kemetism
kemetism.summary: A neopagan religion based on ancient Egyptian beliefs that emerged in the 1970s, ranging from eclectic and reconstructionist approaches to the more monotheistic Kemetic Orthodoxy.

zamalek-sc.name: Zamalek SC
zamalek-sc.summary: An Egyptian sports club founded in 1911, best known for its football team, one of the most widely supported clubs in Africa and the Middle East.

al-ahly-sc.name: Al Ahly SC
al-ahly-sc.summary: A professional sports club based in Cairo, Egypt, founded in 1907, mainly known for football; it is considered the most decorated and successful club in world football.

africa-cup-of-nations.name: Africa Cup of Nations
africa-cup-of-nations.summary: The main biennial international men's football competition in Africa, run by the Confederation of African Football since its first edition in 1957, when only Sudan, Egypt and Ethiopia took part.

cairo-international-film-festival.name: Cairo International Film Festival
cairo-international-film-festival.summary: An annual film festival founded in 1976 and held at the Cairo Opera House, recognized as the oldest competitive feature film festival in Africa and the Arab world.

fiapf.name: FIAPF
fiapf.summary: An international organization of film producers' associations, founded in 1933, that accredits many of the world's major film festivals.

sayed-darwish.name: Sayed Darwish
sayed-darwish.summary: Egyptian singer and composer (1892–1923) regarded as the father of Egyptian popular music and one of the country's greatest musicians.

umm-kulthum.name: Umm Kulthum
umm-kulthum.summary: Egyptian singer and film actress (1904 to 1975), widely regarded as the Arab world's most distinguished 20th-century singer; her Cairo funeral drew over 4 million people.

mohammed-abdel-wahab.name: Mohammed Abdel Wahab
mohammed-abdel-wahab.summary: Egyptian singer and actor (1902–1991) known for romantic and patriotic songs, who also composed Libya's national anthem, used from 1951 to 1969 and again since 2011.

abdel-halim-hafez.name: Abdel Halim Hafez
abdel-halim-hafez.summary: Egyptian singer, actor and film producer (1929–1977), nicknamed 'the Brown-Skinned Nightingale,' regarded as one of the greatest Egyptian musicians of his era, with sales of over 80 million records.

baligh-hamdi.name: Baligh Hamdi
baligh-hamdi.summary: Egyptian composer (1931-1993) who wrote many hit songs for Arab singers especially in the 1960s-70s, including Warda's most famous songs; the two later married.

mutamassirun.name: Mutamassirun
mutamassirun.summary: Term for foreigners, mainly Greeks, Italians, Jews, Armenians and Maltese, living in Egypt chiefly in the 19th and 20th centuries; most left after the 1950s Suez Crisis.

sa-idi-people.name: Sa'idi
sa-idi-people.summary: A term for a person from Upper Egypt.

peter-gabriel.name: Peter Gabriel
peter-gabriel.summary: English singer-songwriter and co-founder of Genesis, who later had a successful solo career including the album So and the protest song "Biko."

world-of-music-arts-and-dance.name: WOMAD
world-of-music-arts-and-dance.summary: An international arts festival and outreach charity celebrating the world's many forms of music, arts and dance.
world-of-music-arts-and-dance.source_title: World of Music, Arts and Dance

fiba-under-19-basketball-world-cup.name: FIBA U19 Basketball World Cup
fiba-under-19-basketball-world-cup.summary: The under-19 men's world basketball championship organized by FIBA, held every four years from 1979 and biennially since 2007.

port-said.name: Port Said
port-said.summary: An Egyptian port city on the Mediterranean at the mouth of the Suez Canal, founded in 1859 during the canal's construction and once home to a cosmopolitan mix of nationalities.

egypt_nubia-modern-culture-002: International Federation of Film Producers Associations
egypt_nubia-modern-culture-005: World of Music and Dance Festival
